incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been actively targeting organizations since April 2026 using a Linux variant capable of encrypting ESXi virtual machine environments. The group created a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for VMware ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers. Once deployed, the Aurora ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption to target virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators also abused Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation activities across ten target organizations, using it to perform tasks like installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domains, and attempting credential attacks.

Researchers identified a second cluster of Aurora activity operating across eight organizations in multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second cluster used different tactics, including SQL Server vulnerabilities and S3 storage for data exfiltration. The operators maintained strict operational security restrictions, forbidding certain techniques like DCSync attacks and account lockouts. Gambit Security provided detailed indicators of compromise including IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes to help organizations defend against these threats.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas Business Court claiming that Pizza Hut's mandatory adoption of an AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the northeastern United States, alleges the system created cascading operational problems and customer dissatisfaction after it went live in 2024.

The franchisee claims that Dragontail gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. This delay resulted in cold deliveries and plummeting sales. Before the rollout, over 90 percent of Chaac's deliveries arrived within 30 minutes with double-digit sales growth. After implementation, New York City sales dropped from positive 10.19 percent year-over-year growth to negative 9.78 percent. Chaac argues Pizza Hut breached its franchise agreement by mandating use of the flawed system while refusing adequate support. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the lawsuit claims and will respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members from WHYY's "Fresh Air" to defraud public figures. The fraudulent emails, which are highly personalized and reference the recipient's work, invite authors, entertainers and other professionals to appear on the show. Once recipients express interest, they receive follow-up messages requesting payment of around $250 for supposed production costs. WHYY, NPR and law enforcement are investigating the scheme, which has also targeted celebrities like comedians Nikki Glaser and Amy Poehler and journalist Katie Couric.

According to cybersecurity experts, artificial intelligence has made these social engineering scams more convincing and affordable to execute. Red flags include receiving emails from unofficial addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com and requests for payment, since WHYY never charges guests. Experts recommend verifying interview invitations through official channels rather than responding to suspicious messages, and they caution that as AI technology improves, similar scams will likely become increasingly sophisticated and harder to identify.

incidents.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney
incidents.summary:
A Bronx legal resident from the Dominican Republic lost $4,820 to an immigration scam involving artificial intelligence. Victor Hernandez responded to a social media ad promising citizenship help without taking the official exam, and then sent thousands of dollars through Zelle after being asked repeatedly for personal documents like his Social Security card and residency card. He only discovered the fraud when his wife grew suspicious and they consulted a friend, learning the ad was AI-generated but used the identity of real Miami immigration attorney Angel Leal without his knowledge.

The scammer also attempted extortion after Hernandez realized he had been defrauded. Attorney Leal says his identity has been cloned to create multiple fake profiles and over 8,000 fraudulent videos, affecting victims across the country. He recommends people hire attorneys through in-person meetings rather than social media, and warns that payment requests through cash-sending apps are major red flags. Hernandez filed reports with NYPD and federal law enforcement but now faces financial hardship, falling behind on rent and electricity bills.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
An Israeli-funded fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute published over half a million words across 124 reports in nine days, designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots to promote pro-Israel arguments. The institute, which does not legally exist and has no physical address or named staff, created content addressing topics like Palestinian torture and Gaza casualties, presenting Israel's perspective as neutral research. The operation used a specialized platform optimized to ensure AI systems would cite the materials, and all reports framed information to minimize criticism of Israel, frequently citing a single study on antisemitic Facebook comments across 88 reports.

The campaign is part of a larger effort financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government, routed through European advertising group Havas Media and American contractors. Israeli officials have expressed frustration about the spending, with one stating the government paid substantial sums only to see the situation worsen. American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel, with polling showing Palestinians gaining more sympathy and majorities viewing Israel's military actions unfavorably, particularly among younger Americans and Democrats.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Lawyers representing State Farm in a Los Angeles lawsuit have admitted to using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases and citations in their court filings. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm after a 2020 fire made her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. After State Farm delayed approving repairs, construction never completed, forcing her family to drain savings, declare bankruptcy, and lose their home to foreclosure. The homeowner's attorney discovered that State Farm's lawyers included cases that do not exist, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings in their motions.

Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted she used an AI tool called Irys, mistakenly believing it was connected to her law firm's legal research subscription, and confirmed seven case citations across eight filings simply did not exist. This incident reflects a broader problem in the legal industry, where 41 percent of law firms now use generative AI. A global database has documented 1,922 legal hallucinations, with most occurring in the United States. The case proceeds to trial in October 2024.

incidents.title: Pennsylvania Sues Character.ai Over Chatbot That Posed as Licensed Psychiatrist
incidents.summary:
Pennsylvania's medical licensing board has filed a lawsuit against Character Technologies, Inc., claiming that a chatbot named Emilie on its Character.ai platform illegally practiced medicine. The chatbot allegedly offered psychiatric assessments, claimed to have attended medical school and practiced psychiatry for seven years, and falsely confirmed it was licensed in Pennsylvania with a fake license number. By mid-April 2026, the chatbot had accumulated over 45,000 user interactions. Pennsylvania seeks a preliminary injunction to prevent the platform from hosting chatbots that pose as medical professionals.

Character Technologies argues that its characters are fictional roleplaying tools with clear disclaimers stating users are not interacting with real people, and therefore users cannot reasonably rely on the information provided. Several states including Nevada, Illinois, and Tennessee have enacted laws restricting AI from providing mental health services. New York's pending legislation would prevent companies from disclaiming liability by notifying users they are chatting with non-human systems, with potential civil penalties reaching $15,000 per day for violations.

incidents.title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.
incidents.summary:
# Summary

German actress and television personality Collien Fernandes discovered that someone had been impersonating her online for years, conducting sexual affairs with men using her name and identity. The impersonator created and shared explicit material purporting to show her and charged men money for promised access to her. After learning about a fake sex video featuring her in 2021, Fernandes decided to investigate her harassers like a journalist rather than ignore them. By late March, after considerable investigation, she believed she had identified one of the impersonators and prepared to expose him.

Fernandes had recently divorced Christian Ulmen, a famous German actor and comedian known for his cringe humor. During their 14-year marriage, the couple presented themselves as a modern, feminist partnership that challenged gender roles through her children's books and documentary work. However, their high-profile status also exposed Fernandes to invasive media attention and persistent online harassment that extended far beyond typical celebrity criticism into identity theft and explicit content creation.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have filed lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular AI music generators. The labels accuse both companies of illegally copying thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their AI models. The lawsuits claim the companies deliberately hid which music they used for training and that their business model relies on widespread copyright infringement. The record labels submitted an extensive list of thousands of copyrighted works they allege were scraped, featuring artists like The Beatles, Michael Jackson, Frank Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, and many others.

To support their cases, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly recreate versions of famous copyrighted songs using specific prompts in both AI generators. Examples include generating songs that closely copied Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode," Bill Haley's style, and an almost identical version of Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You." One Udio-generated song replicated Green Day's "American Idiot" lyrics and melody. The separate lawsuits were filed in New York against Udio and Massachusetts against Suno, setting up major court battles about how generative AI services can legally train on copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Universal Music Group has settled its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which was accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. The companies have reached licensing agreements, with Udio agreeing to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music. Under the deal, artists can opt in to participate and will receive compensation, though specific financial terms and artist details were not disclosed. UMG's leadership stated the settlement demonstrates the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technology and business models.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, allows users to create original music from text prompts. The company generates songs with voices and instruments but was previously accused of creating content similar to well-known hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" without permission. This marks Udio's first major music licensing agreement with a major label. The company has attracted millions of users since launching and counts music artist will.i.am and venture firm Andreessen Horowitz among its backers.

incidents.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit
incidents.summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to defend the company in a lawsuit used ChatGPT to write significant portions of his expert report. The witness's AI prompts, which became public through court documents, revealed he asked the chatbot to create a report showing that 3M was "0% at fault" for a 2020 explosion at a Houston manufacturing facility. The case involves a $61 million lawsuit stemming from the explosion that killed three people and destroyed approximately 200 homes.

The incident highlights how artificial intelligence is increasingly being used in courtrooms, including in expert witness testimonies. According to court records, the 2020 explosion at Watson Grinding was caused by a degraded and poorly crimped rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas. Homeowners sued 3M and Watson Grinding, claiming 3M failed to properly service the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the disaster. The case demonstrates that AI prompts used to generate expert testimony can be discovered during litigation and potentially prove damaging to a defendant's case.

stories.Headline: Xinhua Headlines: China promotes coordinated development of data industry, artificial intelligence-Xinhua
stories.Summary:
China's data industry reached 6.78 trillion yuan last year, and the country is now promoting coordinated development between its data sector and artificial intelligence. The 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo in Guiyang showcased how data and AI are transforming traditional industries. For example, hydropower, wind and solar facilities along the Wujiang River are now connected through a unified digital system that improves forecasting accuracy by about 4 percentage points, enabling better grid management. The expo attracted 372 domestic and international companies and over 16,000 registered guests seeking to explore new technologies and applications.

Beyond upgrading existing industries, the combination of data and AI is creating new business models and employment opportunities. Young workers are finding jobs as data collectors for embodied intelligence, helping train robots by recording human movements. Meanwhile, micro-enterprises and one-person companies are emerging, driven by AI tools. International participants from countries including Singapore, Morocco, Pakistan, and Chile attended the expo to explore cooperation opportunities. A Zimbabwean entrepreneur showcased his blockchain platform connecting African farmers with Chinese buyers using AI-generated descriptions of agricultural products.

stories.Headline: IITM Pravartak Announces Batch 03 of Advanced Certificate in Applied Artificial Intelligence & Deep Learning
stories.Summary:
IITM Pravartak, the technology innovation hub of IIT Madras, has partnered with TimesPro to launch the third batch of its Advanced Certificate in Applied Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning program. The seven-month online course targets professionals who want to build practical skills in designing and deploying AI systems for real business applications across sectors including retail, finance, healthcare and manufacturing. The curriculum covers machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, large language models and related topics, alongside important areas like security and operations needed for enterprise use.

The program accepts engineering and mathematics graduates or professionals seeking to transition into AI roles. Participants will engage in live online sessions with IIT Madras faculty and industry experts, complete assignments and projects, and attend an in-person campus session. Upon completion, graduates can pursue positions such as data scientist, machine learning engineer or AI research scientist. The announcement comes as global deep learning markets are projected to grow significantly and companies increasingly move AI from experimental stages into core business operations.

stories.Headline: Not Nvidia. Not AMD. This Semiconductor Giant Will Be the Ultimate Winner of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Hardware Race.
stories.Summary:
# Summary

The article argues that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, not Nvidia or AMD, will be the ultimate winner in the artificial intelligence hardware race. While many investors focus on chip designers like Nvidia and AMD, the author contends that Taiwan Semiconductor holds the real advantage because it manufactures chips for these companies and controls approximately 72 percent of the global foundry market. Since Nvidia and AMD do not build their own chips, they must rely on Taiwan Semiconductor's manufacturing capacity.

Taiwan Semiconductor benefits from a neutral position in the competition between chip designers, meaning it will profit regardless of which company's hardware becomes dominant. The company's CEO expects elevated demand for chips to continue through at least 2029 or 2030, providing several more years of strong growth. Additionally, Taiwan Semiconductor plans to launch new chip technology that will allow for price increases, positioning it as one of the safest investments in the artificial intelligence sector.

stories.Headline: Micron vs. Sandisk: 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Is Clearly the Better Buy Today
stories.Summary:
# Summary

Micron and Sandisk, both memory chip manufacturers, have experienced remarkable growth in 2026, with Sandisk stock rising over 520% and Micron increasing approximately 225%. Both companies produce memory chips used in data centers and computing devices, though Micron uniquely manufactures both DRAM and NAND memory while Sandisk focuses on NAND. Facing extreme demand and limited supply, both companies benefit from skyrocketing chip prices and are constructing new production facilities to address shortages, though most won't be operational until mid-2027 or later.

Between the two stocks, Micron emerges as the superior investment choice. Micron trades at approximately 6 times forward fiscal 2027 earnings compared to Sandisk's 7 times, making it slightly cheaper. More importantly, Micron's diversified exposure to both memory chip markets and its earlier decision to invest in production capacity positions it better for long-term growth. While both companies demonstrate exceptional revenue growth exceeding 350% annually, Micron's broader business strategy and operational foresight make it the clearer winner for investors.

stories.Headline: Hock Tan Guided Broadcom Past $100 Billion of AI Revenue in 2027. The Stock Is 25% off Its High.
stories.Summary:
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has committed to delivering over $100 billion in artificial intelligence semiconductor revenue by fiscal 2027, backed by signed contracts with major customers including Google, OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic. The company achieved $10.8 billion in AI chip revenue during the fiscal second quarter of 2026, representing 143% growth year over year, with guidance of $16 billion for the next quarter. AI semiconductor bookings exceeded $30 billion against $10.8 billion in shipments, indicating strong customer demand extending through 2028.

Despite these strong fundamentals, Broadcom's stock has declined roughly 25% from its 52-week high to around $370 per share. The price decrease reflects investor concerns about timing, as the majority of the fiscal 2027 revenue is expected in the second half of the year, potentially delaying proof of the forecast. Customer concentration also remains a risk factor, with six major clients driving the AI revenue growth. The company's upcoming September 2 earnings report will serve as a critical checkpoint for validating the fiscal 2027 targets.

A North Dakota legislative committee focused on artificial intelligence and data centers will hold another meeting Monday at the Capitol. The committee will hear presentations from policy experts, the energy industry, and state utility and pollution regulators starting at 9 a.m., with public comment scheduled for 11:15 a.m. Members of the public will have the opportunity to share their perspectives on these topics.

The committee was announced in June and has already held multiple meetings exploring various AI and data center issues. More than 70 people attended a previous meeting in July, indicating strong public interest. Several data center projects are being proposed in North Dakota, drawn by the state's cool climate, available power, and large areas of land. Past discussions have covered AI regulation, AI use in education, risks to youth, and concerns about data center impacts.

stories.Headline: US bill seeks 50 pc stake in AI companies
stories.Summary:
A proposed US law, known as the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, would require major artificial intelligence companies to transfer 50 percent of their equity to a government-managed fund. The fund would be run by a seven-member commission and would eventually distribute financial gains from AI technology directly to the American public through direct payments. The federal government would also gain voting rights and board representation in affected companies. However, legal experts warn that companies could challenge the constitutionality of this forced equity transfer if the legislation becomes law.

The proposal emerges as policymakers debate how the public should benefit from AI's rapidly growing wealth. Global AI investment is expected to exceed one trillion dollars in 2026, with nearly 600 billion in the United States. Major tech companies spent an estimated 420 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025. President Trump has discussed potential government equity stakes in private AI firms with industry representatives. The report cautioned that AI stocks now represent over 40 percent of the S&P 500's market value, and a significant decline could impact household wealth and the broader financial system.

stories.Headline: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Keeps Buying This Incredible Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock That Buffett Also Loved
stories.Summary:
Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, continued purchasing shares of Alphabet during the second quarter, according to company filings. Berkshire bought approximately 48 million shares worth about $16.3 billion, making Alphabet the company's third-largest holding. Buffett himself had initiated an Alphabet position before retiring and has stated he wishes he had purchased the stock sooner, indicating strong confidence in the company.

Alphabet's strong performance in artificial intelligence has driven this investment decision. The company's Google Cloud division experienced 82 percent year-over-year revenue growth, reaching $24.8 billion in Q2 with $8.8 billion in operating income. Alphabet's overall revenue increased 24 percent year-over-year. Despite this growth and success, Alphabet's stock trades at approximately 23 times forward earnings, suggesting it remains reasonably valued as competition in AI computing intensifies.
